Clinical details: Severe aortic stenosis. Previous CABG 2014, CKD stage 3b. TAVI work-up.

Technique: ECG-gated CT angiography of the aortic root and heart, followed by non-gated CT angiography from the thoracic inlet to the lesser trochanters. 60 ml iohexol 350. DLP 583 mGy·cm.

Findings:

Thoracic aorta: Ascending aorta 33 mm. Arch and descending thoracic aorta of normal calibre. No dissection. Sternotomy wires in situ.

Subclavian/axillary arteries: Unremarkable. No significant stenosis. Left internal mammary artery graft patent.

Abdominal aorta: Normal calibre. No abdominal aortic aneurysm. Coeliac axis, SMA and renal arteries patent.

Iliofemoral access (minimal luminal diameter):
Right: CIA 5.2 mm, EIA 5.6 mm, CFA 6.0 mm.
Left: CIA 6.4 mm, EIA 5.4 mm, CFA 5.9 mm.
Calcification: severe, circumferential at the right common iliac artery. Tortuosity: marked bilaterally. No dissection.

Lungs and airways: 4 mm solid nodule in the left upper lobe (series 5, image 63), below the size threshold for follow-up under BTS guidance. No suspicious pulmonary nodule. No consolidation. Airways patent.

Pleura and pericardium: Small bilateral pleural effusions. No pericardial effusion.

Mediastinum: No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy.

Upper abdomen: Unremarkable within the limits of an arterial phase study.

Bones: No aggressive osseous lesion. Degenerative change in the thoracolumbar spine.

Conclusion:
1. Iliofemoral access: small calibre bilaterally; minimal luminal diameter right common iliac artery 5.2 mm with severe circumferential calcification, left external iliac artery 5.4 mm; marked tortuosity.
2. Small bilateral pleural effusions.

Transfemoral access is likely to be challenging; alternative access may need to be discussed at the heart team meeting.

Annular sizing, valve morphology, coronary ostial heights and aortic root measurements are reported separately in the structural heart report; please refer to that report for valve planning.
